cards.explanation: The answer is that none of them falls short of it. The writer says, "Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it." (Hebrews 4:1) Notice he says "let us." He puts himself right in there with the readers. Nobody gets left standing at the counter alone, friends.

The answer is that they did not share the faith of those who understood it. The writer says the message they heard was of no value to them, "…since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it." (Hebrews 4:2) They heard the same good news the readers did, friends. The difference was faith. Hearing it wasn't enough.

The word is believed. The writer says, "Now we who have believed enter that rest." (Hebrews 4:3) It lines up with verse 2, where the others lacked faith. Simple, clear, and no secret recipe needed, friends.

The answer is True. The writer says God has spoken somewhere about the seventh day. Then he quotes it: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.” (Hebrews 4:4) So he really does point back to creation, just like the card says, friends.

The answer is to not harden their hearts. God says through David, "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts." (Hebrews 4:7) Hearing His voice is the moment that matters, friends. A hard heart is the thing to avoid.

The answer is False. The writer says, "For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day." (Hebrews 4:8) God did speak later about another day, friends. So the rest the writer means wasn't already given by Joshua.

The word is work. The writer says, "For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His." (Hebrews 4:10) The pattern is God's own rest, friends. He rested from His works, and whoever enters His rest rests from his own.

The answer is so no one falls by following the same pattern of disobedience. The writer says, "Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience." (Hebrews 4:11) The pattern he means is the one from the wilderness people, friends. He wants nobody to fall the way they did.

The answer is the thoughts and intentions of the heart. The writer says the word of God "…judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart." (Hebrews 4:12) It goes deep, friends, all the way to soul and spirit, joints and marrow. Nothing in there stays out of reach.

The answer is True. The writer says everything is uncovered and exposed "…before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account." (Hebrews 4:13) The verse says it plainly, friends. God is the One we give account to.
